In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hysterectomy appears to be a normalised treatment option for gynecological ailments, particularly among low-income women with few resources or awareness of possible side effects.
hysterectomy is an important and common treatment for gynaecal ailments in rural, low-income India.
the decision to undergo a hysterectomy is influenced by a complex set of individual, household, socioeconomic and health system factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the study found that women in rural Gujarat were undergoing hysterectomy at an early age, as a permanent solution to gynaecological problems.

the decision to undergo permanent surgical solutions for gynaecologic ailments reflects the embedded social inequality in which women negotiate medical treatment and the need to reverse this culture of permanent solutions in low income settings.

women's experiences of hysterectomy in this setting reflect the power structures and gender inequalities in which they negotiated medical treatment--a pragmatic solution to a long-standing, permanent solution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hysterectomy, in its current form, is not an appropriate treatment for women in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs).
